newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Lynrock buys control of Team Concepts.
newsitem.headline: Lynrock buys control of Team Concepts.

text.p: Team Concepts Holdings Ltd said on Monday its major shareholders had agreed to sell their combined 46.3 percent stake, or 104.27 million shares, in the company to third party Lynrock Corp at HK$0.15 per share.
Lynrock would then make a general cash offer of HK$0.15 each for all Team Concepts shares, the company said in a statement
The deal values the manufacturer of telephones and electronic educational products at HK$33.80 million.
Lynrock would also subscribe to HK$30 million worth of notes convertible into Team Concepts shares at an initial subscription price of HK$0.15 each subject to adjustment.

"The group has continued to experience difficult business conditions in the telecommunication products business and now requires an urgent infusion of working capital for daily operation of the group," Team Concepts said.
The selling shareholders were Holystone Ltd, Hambrook Ltd and King's Union Corp.

Team Concepts said the net proceeds of the note issue would be used for general working capital. Assuming full conversion of the note, Team Concepts would be required to issue 200 million new shares, representing 47.02 percent of the enlarged share capital.
Lynrock's stake in Team Concepts would be raised to 71.54 percent from 46.3 percent on conversion of the note.
Lynrock, which expects to appoint new directors, said it has no intention of changing Team Concepts core business or personnel, or injecting assets into the company.
Lynrock is owned 51 percent by Chan Cher Boon, 29 percent by Ng Siong Tee and 20 percent by Chan Toh Pew.
Chan Cher Boon is a director of Wah Shing Toys International Ltd and Van Der Horst Ltd. Ng is the general manager of Kontiki Shipping Pte Ltd in Singapore.

Chan Toh Pew is the managing director of Balson Ltd, a manufacturer of drinks and juices in Hong Kong and China. Trading in shares of Team Concepts was suspended on February 26 and is due to resume on Monday.
Its shares closed at HK$0.33 each on February 25.
